It's just gotten to the point where I feel completely drained all the time, and I really need some help figuring out how to fix it.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, alongside your sleep disturbances?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've had this deep, heavy feeling of emptiness and hopelessness for over two years now. I constantly feel worthless, like I'm just a burden to everyone around me, and it's always there right alongside my sleep struggles. It has made it incredibly hard for me to function or do anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if your feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, as well as your sleep disturbances, have been constant over the past two years or if they have fluctuated in severity?\n\nPatient: They have been incredibly constant, and I can't remember the last time that heavy, hopeless feeling lifted for more than a day or two. While other things might fluctuate slightly, the terrible sleep and this deep exhaustion have been a persistent, daily struggle ever since my breakup.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned your symptoms started after a breakup; can you tell me more about how your symptoms have related to significant life events or stressors over the past two years?\n\nPatient: Everything started a little over two years ago after a painful breakup with my boyfriend and a stressful conflict with my parents about me staying in northern Alabama. The heavy depression, lack of interest, and exhaustion have been there almost constantly since then. The paranoid feelings of being monitored and hearing that male voice actually started several months later and have been coming and going for over a year now.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood and energy levels that lasted for at least two months since your symptoms started, or have your symptoms been consistently present without any notable periods of remission?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any periods of improvement like that at all. The heavy, hopeless feeling and total lack of energy have been consistently there almost every single day for the past two years. Even on the rare occasion I have a slightly better day, it only lasts for a day or two before I sink right back down.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned having paranoid feelings of being monitored and hearing a male voice; can you tell me more about when these symptoms occur and how often you experience them?\n\nPatient: I hear the male voice a few times a week, mostly at night when I'm alone in my apartment. The feeling that my ex and parents are monitoring me through my coworkers started a few months after the breakup and has been coming and going for over a year. It even happened during a stretch last fall when my mood felt relatively neutral and I wasn't feeling quite as depressed.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear is real, or do you think it might be a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: When it's happening, the voice feels incredibly real and terrifying, and I'll actually get up to check every room in my apartment. Logically, I know there is nobody there, so I suspect it must be a product of my own mind or all this stress. But in the moment, it is really hard to convince myself of that.\n\nDoctor: When you have these feelings of being monitored, do you think they are based on facts or evidence that you can see or prove, or do they seem more like fears or suspicions that you can't shake?\n\nPatient: Logically, I know I can't prove it and that it probably sounds completely paranoid. But the suspicion is so strong that I just can't shake the feeling that my ex and my parents are quietly feeding information about me to people at my job. Even though there's no concrete evidence, it feels very real to me when I'm at work.\n\nDoctor: When you're experiencing these feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, do the voices or paranoid feelings seem to be directly related to your mood, or do they seem to be separate experiences?\n\nPatient: It actually feels like both. But they can also be separate, like last fall when my mood felt pretty neutral but I still heard the voice and felt monitored.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period where your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, significantly improved, but the hallucinations or paranoid delusions persisted?\n\nPatient: Yes, last fall there was a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt relatively neutral and I didn't feel as sad or drained. Even though the heavy depression lifted during that time, I still kept hearing the male voice at night and remained convinced that my family and my ex were watching me through my coworkers.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the male voice you hear and the feelings of being monitored relate to each other, and do they ever seem to be triggered by specific events or stressors?\n\nPatient: They are closely linked because the male voice I hear actually tells me that I'm being watched and that I'm a burden. They often happen at the same time, particularly when I'm alone in my apartment at night or when my depression is at its worst. They originally started a few months after my breakup and family conflict, and they always seem to flare up when I am feeling highly stressed, empty, or overwhelmed.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the male voice you hear and the feelings of being monitored are part of your own thoughts and feelings, or do they seem to be imposed on you from outside, like something is forcing you to think or hear these things?\n\nPatient: The male voice sounds like a real, physical person speaking to me from somewhere in the room, which is why I physically get up to check instead of it just feeling like an internal thought. As for the monitoring, it feels like a real external plot being carried out around me, but I don't feel like some outside force is physically forcing thoughts into my head or controlling my mind directly.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where the hallucinations or paranoid delusions were the predominant symptoms, and your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness, were less prominent or even absent?\n\nPatient: Yes, that happened during that stretch last fall I mentioned. For about two weeks, my depressive symptoms were mostly absent and my mood felt relatively neutral, but the male voice at night and the feeling of being monitored were still just as strong.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where the male voice you hear provides commentary on your actions or thoughts, or seems to be conversing with you, rather than just making statements about being watched or being a burden?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't actually converse with me or comment on what I'm doing. It only ever repeats those specific, scary statements about me being a burden or being watched. It's always just those same repetitive phrases, usually when I'm alone in my apartment at night.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts, feelings, or actions are being controlled or influenced by an external force or power?\n\nPatient: No, I have never felt like an external force is controlling or influencing my thoughts or actions. Even when I hear the voice or feel paranoid, my thoughts and decisions still feel entirely like my own.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there are any times when you feel like the male voice is responding to your thoughts or if it seems to know things about you that you haven't told anyone?\n\nPatient: No, it doesn't ever respond to my thoughts or reveal any secrets. It just tells me that I'm a burden or that I'm being watched, which still makes me get up and check every room even though I know no one is there.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any significant disorganization in your thinking or behavior, such as difficulty maintaining a logical flow of thoughts or engaging in aimless or purposeless activities?\n\nPatient: Yes, sometimes at work I'll find myself standing completely frozen in the hallway or by the copier, just staring into space. I feel totally unable to move or figure out what I'm supposed to be doing next until a coworker snaps me out of it.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the male voice you hear and the feelings of being monitored are always consistent with your depressive mood, or if there are times when these experiences seem unrelated to how you're feeling emotionally?\n\nPatient: While they usually pile on together during my worst depressive periods, there are definitely times when they happen independently of my mood.
